title: I Posted the School Pickup Lane Photo After They Blocked the Crosswalk

parts.text: I walked the crosswalk at 3:12 p.m. with my first grader and a Tahoe stopped on the stripes while the driver scrolled. The school's own flyer, emailed yesterday, said never block the crosswalk. I was thirty-eight, on foot by choice. I photographed the plate, the stripes, and the flyer on my phone. Then I sent it to the principal's pickup address, which they published. At 3:16 the driver yelled that parents photograph other parents now, still on the stripes, as a crossing guard blew a whistle that had been ignored.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The whistle is blowing and she is yelling about photos from the stripes.

social.video_title: Yesterday's flyer, today's Tahoe on the stripes — Part 1/2
social.description: First grader, published email, scrolling driver. Would you have walked behind the SUV?

parts.text: The principal forwarded a reminder with the photo cropped to the stripes, no plate. The driver still knew. Pickup cones moved farther back. We walked. The whistle got respect for a week, which is a start. Flyers are not decorations. Crosswalks are not waiting rooms. My kid still holds my hand. I still have the uncropped version. I do not post plates in parent Facebook. I post them to the address they asked for.

social.description: Reminder email, a week of whistle, hand-holding. Was scrolling a lane?
